questions.q: Why does this lesson say identity is the governance layer everything else depends on?
options: You can't meaningfully restrict access, enforce policy, or produce useful audit logs for a principal the system can't reliably identify
Because identity is the only layer that cloud providers actually bill for
Because policy and monitoring are optional once identity is configured correctly
Because data classification automatically happens once identity is set up
questions.explain: Access restrictions, policy enforcement, and audit logging all require a trustworthy way to know who's asking — without reliable identity, every downstream governance control inherits that weakness.

questions.q: What is a "principal" in cloud IAM terminology?
options: Anything that can be granted permissions — a human user, a group, an application, or a service identity
Only a human user with administrator-level access
A synonym for a cloud subscription or account
A term used only in AWS, with no equivalent concept in Azure
questions.explain: A principal is any entity that permissions can be granted to, which includes users, groups, applications, and service identities like an Azure managed identity or an AWS IAM role assumed by a service.

questions.q: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
options: Authentication proves who you are; authorization determines what you're allowed to do once authenticated
They are two different names for exactly the same process
Authentication only applies to humans; authorization only applies to applications
Authorization happens before authentication in every cloud IAM system
questions.explain: Authentication (AuthN) is proving identity; authorization (AuthZ) is the subsequent determination of what that identity is permitted to do. Both happen, in that order, on every request.

questions.q: How does Azure structurally split identity, compared to AWS?
options: Azure splits it into Microsoft Entra ID (authentication/directory identity) and Azure RBAC (resource-level authorization); AWS handles both in one service, IAM
Azure and AWS use the exact same single-service model for identity
AWS splits identity into two services while Azure uses just one
Neither cloud distinguishes between authentication and authorization at all
questions.explain: Azure separates authentication/directory identity (Entra ID) from resource-level authorization (Azure RBAC) into two distinct services, while AWS IAM handles both concerns within a single unified service.

questions.q: Which Azure service would answer the question "can this user delete this storage account"?
options: Azure RBAC
Microsoft Entra ID
AWS IAM
Neither service — that question isn't answerable in Azure
questions.explain: A question about what an identity is allowed to do to a specific resource is a resource-level authorization question, which is Azure RBAC's job — not Entra ID's, which handles authentication and directory-level identity.
